name: Breeze block
summary: A hollow concrete block with a pierced pattern; a wall of them shades and lets air and light through.
how: Use blocks of 300 to 400mm square with 40% to 60% open area.
Stack the blocks in one grid of one pattern; mix no more than 2 patterns in one wall.
Inside, use the screen to divide zones while it keeps light and air.

origin.note: Three engineers in Recife patent the cobogó, a hollow concrete block for screen walls in a hot climate.

adoptions.via: Tropical modernism and desert houses in the United States use screen walls; Edward Durell Stone wraps the US Embassy in New Delhi (1959) in a pierced screen.
Breeze-block room dividers, bar fronts and planters move inside the house.

sources.title: Edward Durell Stone, United States Embassy, New Delhi (1959)
